Deutsche Telekom Lifts Guidance and Dividend as Broker Price Targets Diverge
sum: Deutsche Telekom has given investors two reasons to look past a subdued share price, raising both its full-year profit outlook and its proposed payout. The stock added 0.4% yesterday, a modest move that masks a busier week of news on networks, artificial intelligence and analyst revisions.

At the centre of the story are the third-quarter figures published on 5 November 2026. Organic revenue grew 5.5% to EUR 31.1 billion, while adjusted EBITDA AL climbed 8.0% organically to EUR 12.2 billion. Those numbers came with upgraded guidance: management now expects adjusted EBITDA AL of around EUR 47.6 billion for 2026, alongside free cash flow AL of roughly EUR 20.1 billion.

Shareholders are in line for a higher distribution. The board intends to propose a dividend of EUR 1.10 per share to the annual general meeting scheduled for 14 April 2027 — a proposal rather than a payment already approved.

Analyst reaction has been mixed. Barclays lifted its price target for the stock from EUR 32 to EUR 33 on Wednesday, with Mathieu Robilliard reaffirming an "Overweight" rating on the back of the strong results. His note carried a caveat, however: investor sentiment has been weighed down by the prospect of satellite-based competition for T-Mobile US.
Goldman Sachs moved the other way. According to media reports, the bank trimmed its target from EUR 38 to EUR 36 on 6 November, while keeping its buy recommendation intact.

On the operational front, the group reported the start of fibre-optic build-out in Wismar, a project that will make connections possible for 2,406 households and businesses. The company was careful to describe these as potential connections rather than lines already in place.

Further expansion in Bavaria is under review, though no final investment decision has been taken on those additional plans. What is already funded is the enlargement of the AI factory in Munich's Tucherpark to 20 megawatts, announced on Monday at a cost of just under a further quarter of a billion euros. The build-out adds NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra systems to the site.

sum: - xStocks brings the DAX 40 onchain, opening Germany’s largest listed companies to 24/7 global trading on 360X.

Tokenized DAX 40 equities are now available on 360X, an affiliated company of Deutsche Börse Group, alongside Xetra-Gold as an xStock. This opens up onchain distribution for Europe’s largest gold security with physical backing. In addition to the recently announced 24/7 trading of DAX 40 equities, it extends distribution to digital-native investors.

xStocks, the tokenized equities framework developed by Payward, has deployed tokenized equities representing every constituent of the DAX 40, Germany’s benchmark stock index. The launch brings onchain the 40 largest blue-chip companies listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and puts them within reach of investors in more than 110 markets. The exchange is operated under Deutsche Börse Group, Payward’s strategic partner.

Each xStock is backed 1:1 by the underlying share, held by a regulated custodian, and tradable 24/7 across select venues. Tokenized versions of SAP (SAPx), Siemens (SIEx), Allianz (ALV.DEx), Deutsche Telekom (DTE.DEx) and others are available from day one. For many investors around the world, this expansion is the first practical way to gain exposure to German capital markets. It also gives the companies themselves a new distribution channel into a global pool of onchain investors, whose demand feeds back to the underlying shares.

Deutsche Telekom's Earnings Momentum Faces a Two-Front Test: SpaceX Competition and a Slimmer Buybac
sum: Deutsche Telekom delivered a quarter that few could fault on operating grounds, yet the market's verdict hinged on something else entirely: the size of the cheque it plans to hand back to shareholders. The Bonn-based group reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of EUR 31.1 billion on November 5, an organic advance of 5.5%, alongside a 12.7% jump in adjusted net profit to EUR 3.0 billion. Investors, however, trained their attention on the capital-return package — and found it wanting.

Adjusted EBITDA AL for the quarter came in at EUR 12.2 billion, up 8.0% organically, meaning earnings grew faster than the top line. Free cash flow AL edged 1.4% higher to EUR 5.7 billion. Those figures underpinned an upgraded full-year outlook: roughly EUR 47.6 billion in adjusted EBITDA AL and around EUR 20.1 billion in free cash flow AL for 2026.

The board also proposed a dividend of EUR 1.10 per share and unveiled share buybacks of up to EUR 2 billion for 2027. By media accounts, both the payout and the repurchase fell short of what the market had pencilled in, and the shortfall — rather than the raised guidance — drove the negative share-price reaction. The average analyst expectation for the buyback had stood at EUR 3 billion, according to press reports, leaving a EUR 1 billion gap that the modestly improved forecast failed to bridge.

Disappointment over capital returns was not the only drag. dpa-AFX attributed part of last week's selling pressure to concerns about potential competition from SpaceX, a threat that lands squarely on T-Mobile US — the group's most important earnings engine. Should those fears crystallise, investors could start valuing future profits more cautiously.

The two risks operate on different planes. The buyback question speaks to what shareholders receive today; the SpaceX question touches on what the business can earn tomorrow. A durable recovery would require the operating trend to be convincing enough to offset both reservations at once. Were weaker results to lend credence to the competitive worries, even the impressive growth rates reported so far could lose their persuasive power.
For the optimistic reading to hold, Deutsche Telekom must show that the recent surge in earnings is more than a snapshot.

Deutsche Telekom Lifts Guidance a Third Time as Q3 Profit Climbs 12.7% and Munich AI Site Sells Out
sum: Deutsche Telekom's third-quarter report card, released on 5 November, showed an adjusted net profit of EUR 3.0 billion for the 2026 period — a 12.7% year-on-year increase — alongside group revenue of EUR 31.1 billion.

Adjusted EBITDA after lease costs came in at EUR 12.2 billion, representing organic growth of 8.0%. That performance underpinned the group's decision, taken roughly a week before the results, to raise its full-year 2026 guidance for the third time this year: management now targets around EUR 47.6 billion in adjusted EBITDA AL and roughly EUR 20.1 billion in free cash flow AL.

Shareholders were offered a dividend of EUR 1.10 per share for the 2026 financial year, with the board also flagging a share buyback of up to EUR 2 billion for 2027. The two measures together form the core of the capital-return package announced alongside the quarterly figures.

On the infrastructure side, the company said on Monday that it would expand its Industrial AI Cloud in Munich's Tucherpark to 20 megawatts, committing just under a further quarter of a billion euros to the project. The first construction phase is already fully booked, according to the group.

Analyst reaction has been mixed. Barclays lifted its price target for the stock from EUR 32 to EUR 33 on the day of the results, keeping an "Overweight" rating. The British bank's stance is tempered by competitive pressure on T-Mobile US from satellite communications providers, which it says continues to weigh on investor sentiment despite the strong quarterly numbers.

Goldman Sachs moved the other way about a week earlier, on Friday, cutting its target from EUR 38 to EUR 36 while maintaining a "Buy" rating. DZ Bank also revised its assessment following the nine-month report and the slightly upgraded outlook, lowering its fair value from EUR 35 to EUR 33 on 5 November but leaving its "Kaufen" (Buy) rating intact.
The shares were up 0.3% at EUR 26.10 in the session following the Barclays note.

With the stock still trading around telecom-level valuations, the open question is how well that current price lines up with the cash the business is expected to generate over time.
- The share price is down 9.4% year to date, so anyone looking at Telefónica Deutschland now is effectively reassessing what that move says about the durability and value of its future cash flows.

SPCX Stock Logs 2-Day Winning Streak: Barclays Calls T-Mobile 'Cleanest' Fit For Potential SpaceX Buyout
sum: - T-Mobile already partners with SpaceX on satellite service but opposes a broader MVNO arrangement.
- SpaceX’s Qualcomm-powered terrestrial 5G rollout is expected to begin in 2027, while Musk remains open to acquisitions.
- Buying a carrier could give SpaceX spectrum, infrastructure and customer operations, while saving time.

Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) rose 6% on Monday, extending their winning streak to two sessions, as Barclays said T-Mobile US (TMUS) could offer the strongest strategic fit if Elon Musk pursues a major wireless acquisition. As SpaceX prepares to launch its own nationwide terrestrial 5G network in 2027, Barclays believes acquiring an established carrier could help accelerate that ambition.
SPCX stock jumped to $142.07 on Monday, posting its second consecutive session in the green.
Barclays said U.S. carriers face a trade-off: selling spare network capacity to SpaceX could bring in revenue while helping a future rival.

“That is the prisoner’s dilemma we have highlighted in our prior notes as, individually, each incumbent benefits from monetizing unused network capacity through wholesale but, collectively, they benefit from denying SpaceX terrestrial access,” the brokerage said, according to Barron’s.

Deutsche Telekom's Solid Quarter Meets a Muted Reception as Buyback Falls Short
sum: Deutsche Telekom delivered a quarter that beat expectations on both revenue and operating profit, yet its shares couldn't hold their pre-market gains and at one point shed more than three percent. The sticking point, according to market reports cited by Reuters, was the size of the buyback the company has earmarked for 2027: at up to EUR 2 billion, it came in below the average analyst estimate of EUR 3 billion, as dpa-AFX noted. The proposed dividend of EUR 1.10 per share for the 2026 financial year also landed slightly short of what the market had been hoping for.

Goldman Sachs lowered its price target for the stock on Friday to EUR 36 from EUR 38, while reaffirming its "Buy" rating. Analyst Andrew Lee revised his estimates to reflect the quarterly report, updated forecasts for T-Mobile US and recent currency movements. The DZ Bank followed suit a day earlier, cutting its fair value to EUR 33 from EUR 35 but sticking with its buy recommendation. Its reassessment was prompted by the nine-month report and the group's slightly raised outlook.

Underneath the payout disappointment, the operating picture remained robust. Third-quarter 2026 revenue reached EUR 31.1 billion, a rise of 5.5 percent on an organic basis. Adjusted EBITDA AL climbed 8.0 percent organically to EUR 12.2 billion, and adjusted net profit came in at EUR 3.0 billion — up 12.7 percent year on year.

Those figures gave management the confidence to lift full-year guidance. Deutsche Telekom now expects adjusted EBITDA AL of around EUR 47.6 billion for 2026, with free cash flow AL of roughly EUR 20.1 billion. Investors will get the full picture on February 25, 2027, when the company reports fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 results.

Away from the numbers, the group had operational news to trumpet. It reported first place in Computer BILD's mobile network test, claiming its 15th consecutive victory in the comparison with an overall grade of "very good (1.2)."

On Wednesday the company also unveiled the "Telekom Equipment Exchange," a platform through which its national subsidiaries can pass on and reuse surplus network equipment internally. The offering is aimed at the group's own country companies and at hardware that can be redeployed within the group.

Deutsche Telekom Lifts 2026 Targets as Q3 Profit Climbs and AI Deals Pile Up
sum: Deutsche Telekom capped a busy week of quarterly reporting and partnership announcements by raising its full-year outlook, with Europe's largest telecoms group now guiding toward a adjusted EBITDA AL of roughly EUR 47.6 billion for 2026 and free cash flow AL of about EUR 20.1 billion.

The upgrade came alongside third-quarter figures showing adjusted net profit up 12.7% to EUR 3.0 billion. Revenue for the period reached EUR 31.1 billion, an organic advance of 5.5%, while adjusted EBITDA AL — earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation after lease costs — rose 8.0% on an organic basis to EUR 12.2 billion. Reported growth outpaced the organic rates, with revenue up 7.5% and adjusted EBITDA AL ahead by 9.9%.
Shareholder returns featured prominently in the board's presentation. Management is planning a dividend of EUR 1.10 per share and has earmarked as much as EUR 2 billion for share buybacks in 2027.
Deutsche Bank Research kept its "Buy" rating on the stock following the results, reiterating a EUR 40 price target.

The quarter's commercial momentum was matched by progress on the technology front. T-Systems, the group's enterprise IT arm, signed a memorandum of understanding with Sparxity at the Digital Summit on Tuesday covering cooperation on energy-efficient AI computing infrastructure. Under the plan, Sparxity's next chip generation would be deployed in Telekom data centres in 2028.

That agreement builds on a separate arrangement disclosed on 28 October, when Banco Sabadell and T-Systems agreed to expand the lender's use of agent-based AI. The Spanish bank will draw on T-Systems' "T-AI Agentic Hub" platform.
Telekom is keeping the AI theme front and centre. A press conference on "AI Factory 2.0" is scheduled for 9 November from 10:00 in Munich, with AI infrastructure for Germany and Europe on the agenda.

Deutsche Telekom's Q3 Beat Draws a Split Verdict From the Analyst Community
sum: Deutsche Telekom's third-quarter 2026 results landed with a solid beat on both the top and bottom lines, yet the analyst reaction that followed was anything but uniform. DZ Bank trimmed its fair value estimate for the shares from EUR 35 to EUR 33 on the back of the nine-month report, while keeping its rating at "Buy." The move pairs a lower valuation level with an unchanged positive recommendation — a cut to the price target, not to the investment case.

JPMorgan took the opposite tack on the same set of numbers, reaffirming "Overweight" with a EUR 38 target. Deutsche Bank Research stayed at "Buy" with EUR 40, and a further house held its own target at EUR 28.10. Among the confirmed views sit both a buy recommendation and a neutral rating, so the Street's verdict is one of agreement on the quarter's quality rather than on the price it justifies.

The operating figures explain why most analysts left their ratings alone. Group revenue for the quarter came in at EUR 31.102 billion, up 7.5% year on year. Adjusted EBITDA AL climbed 9.9% to EUR 12.210 billion, and adjusted net profit reached EUR 3.008 billion, a gain of 12.7%.

That the bottom line grew faster than the top line is the signal bulls are leaning on. Whether the trend can be repeated is the question that now matters for the investment case — a single strong quarter only justifies a more favourable view if it feeds into a durable outlook for the periods ahead.

Management reinforced that expectation by lifting full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA AL to around EUR 47.6 billion. Free cash flow AL is now projected at roughly EUR 20.1 billion for 2026. The board also intends to propose a dividend of EUR 1.10 per share for the financial year, with share buybacks of up to EUR 2 billion earmarked for 2027.

Those two guidance figures serve different purposes: the operating result describes earnings momentum, while the cash flow line measures the financial room to manoeuvre. Investors would find the story most convincing if both held up together. For now they remain forecasts, not delivered full-year outcomes.
The same caution applies to the payout plans. A proposed dividend is not yet an approved distribution, and the announced buyback volume is a ceiling rather than a completed purchase.

Deutsche Telekom's Fiber Reach Hits 14.4 Million Homes — Earnings Must Show It Converts
sum: Deutsche Telekom has spent the autumn stacking up operational wins. On November 5, 2026, it has to demonstrate that they add up to money.

The Bonn-based group will publish third-quarter 2026 figures that morning, with a press conference scheduled for 10 a.m. For shareholders, the report is less about any single announcement than about whether the operating story carries financial weight on its own — without a fresh corporate transaction to lean on.

The build-out numbers are the headline act. Deutsche Telekom reported on October 27 that September alone brought 255,000 additional fiber connections, lifting the total footprint to 14.4 million households and businesses able to sign up for fiber tariffs. Mobile infrastructure moved too: 72 new sites went live in September, and capacity was expanded at 503 existing ones.

None of this implies Deutsche Telekom has already reported weakness. It is simply the line investors need to draw between technical progress and its financial effect. The next report should be read for evidence that business development and management commentary support that link. Another month of build-out gains would be welcome, but it would not settle the question by itself. By the same token, a convincing commercial performance need not hinge on a single monthly coverage statistic — what matters is reach and usage working together.

A solid operating quarter would give the optimistic reading real substance. So would the surrounding news flow, which has been constructive. JPMorgan reaffirmed its "Overweight" rating and EUR 38 price target on Thursday — a confirmation rather than an upgrade or a raised target, supportive of the bullish view but no fresh operating proof of it.

New mandates point in the same direction, if cautiously. The European Central Bank selected Deutsche Telekom Business Solutions and Nexi Payments jointly as network service providers for the digital euro. Reported roughly a week ago, the assignment initially covers pilot operations — a concrete task, though not yet the business of full-scale rollout.

Buybacks add another layer. For the most recently reported purchase period, Deutsche Telekom disclosed 6,017,301 repurchased shares yesterday, bringing the total since the program began to 44,155,725.

sum: Deutsche Telekom shares fell 3.7% yesterday, and the cause was not a profit warning, a downgrade, or any fresh disclosure from the company itself. It was a report about a company that does not yet compete with it — and may not for years.

Reuters, citing Bloomberg, reported that SpaceX is in talks to secure access to at least 80,000 US mobile sites, a move that would give its ambitions a concrete infrastructural footing. None of the parties involved has confirmed the discussions. That distinction matters more than the headline number: what investors sold was exposure to a possible fourth US network, not evidence of a network already running.
The link to Bonn runs through T-Mobile US, the American subsidiary in which Deutsche Telekom holds a majority stake. No operational update accompanied the slide. The stock moved on perception.

Analysts at Bernstein pushed back on the idea that competitive damage is imminent, arguing that real consequences could be years away. Their note nonetheless conceded that progress on spectrum and infrastructure is already weighing on sector sentiment — a gap that captures the whole problem. Valuations reprice in a single session; businesses take far longer to feel the effect.

That gap has a mechanical side. Reuters also reported a SpaceX agreement to purchase a nationwide portfolio of low-band spectrum licences, a deal that could position Starlink Mobile as a major US telecoms operator. Spectrum plus sites is the combination that turns a satellite story into a terrestrial threat — at least on paper.

The financials involved are substantial. TD Cowen estimates the cost of building a nationwide network at more than $80bn. That figure guarantees nothing about timing, but it makes plain that site access alone does not finish the job. A multi-year build-out would give T-Mobile US room to respond on its own schedule rather than overnight.

Barclays had already trimmed its price target for Deutsche Telekom on Tuesday, cutting it from EUR 35 to EUR 32 while keeping an "Overweight" rating. The bank flagged satellite-based offerings and AI systems as sector risks. A lower target paired with an unchanged positive rating is a long-horizon adjustment, not a rush for the exits — a different animal from the selling that followed the US reports.

sum: The math facing Deutsche Telekom investors is deceptively simple on paper: roughly €20 billion in projected free cash flow, a buyback program now swollen to €5 billion, and an AI strategy still waiting to be priced in. The hard part comes on October 5, when management steps up in Bonn to explain how all three ambitions fit together.

That presentation, billed as an "AI Investor Day," arrives at a delicate moment. The stock has already climbed 10.31 percent over the past 30 days, powered by last Friday's ad-hoc announcement that the 2026 buyback program would be topped up by €3 billion. The additional tranches began executing this week and are scheduled to run through December 22. But the market's real question is whether the capital being returned to shareholders will starve the investment needs that the AI agenda will inevitably bring.

The second quarter offered plenty of raw material for the bulls. Group revenue rose 4.4 percent to €29.9 billion, while net profit climbed 11.1 percent to €2.8 billion. Free cash flow advanced 3.1 percent to €5.0 billion — a figure that looks all the more resilient given that T-Mobile US, the group's American engine, has shown signs of softening.

The German home market delivered its own encouraging details. Segment revenue grew 3.7 percent to €6.5 billion, and the broadband mix continued its structural shift: traditional connections fell by 20,000, but fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) lines added 161,000. The churn toward faster infrastructure is reshaping the customer base even as the overall broadband count edges lower.

Friday's announcement did more than expand the repurchase program. Management also lifted the full-year free cash flow guidance to approximately €20 billion, a move grounded in an upgraded outlook from T-Mobile US. The combination of a larger buyback and a higher cash flow forecast suggests Bonn sees room to reward shareholders without choking off investment capacity.

Analysts have taken notice. JPMorgan and Deutsche Bank both reaffirmed their views after the quarterly release, and consensus estimates point to roughly 37 percent upside from current levels. The stock, however, remains 15.87 percent below its 52-week high of €34.35, reached in late February.

The Siren Song of the Golden Share: The Troubled History of Government Equity in Technology
sum: OpenAI’s proposal to hand the U.S. government a 5 percent equity stake has made a theoretical debate over the relationship between private corporations and the government into an immediately relevant policy question. Coupled with Sen. Bernie Sanders’ (I-Vt.) proposal that the federal government acquire a 50 percent ownership stake in the top American artificial intelligence (AI) firms—a radical idea that has received an ally in President Trump—we are now at a critical moment that could have serious implications for the future competitiveness of the United States in AI development.

A recent R Street analysis laid out a definitive case for why any form of government control over AI would represent a fundamental threat to American innovation, competitiveness, and freedom of expression, regardless of whether the approach was “hard” nationalization or “soft” equity arrangements. Due to the increasing prevalence of dialogue surrounding the U.S. government taking equity in private companies, it is important to understand there is a well-documented history that accompanies these efforts, with a consistent outcome. Government ownership of transformative technology companies reliably produces stagnation, cronyism, and competitive decline—none of which are acceptable when it comes to AI development.

The main mechanism discussed surrounding proposals for AI companies is the partial equity stake. Known as the “golden share,” it is proposed as a middle path between full nationalization and genuine market independence. The historical record could not be more clear: Even minority ownership, when paired with political influence over business decisions, functions as a powerful control mechanism regardless of the equity percentage. Governments with golden shares are not passive observers. They consistently intervene and in doing so elevate political calculation above commercial and technological judgment.
Advocates for government equity will likely invoke developmentalism, an economic theory that state-directed capital allocation can build strategic industries that markets alone would not produce.

items.t: Can T-Mobile Survive Starlink's Spectrum Siege? for NASDAQ:TMUS by UDIS_View
sum: The competitive moat protecting T-Mobile (TMUS) is eroding rapidly as SpaceX completes a transformational $20 billion spectrum acquisition from EchoStar, securing over 65 megahertz of mid-band frequencies. This consolidation removes Starlink's structural dependency on terrestrial mobile network operators and positions SpaceX to launch its own retail cellular service. The exclusive direct-to-cell partnership between T-Mobile and Starlink expires next month, and SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell has confirmed the company is actively evaluating direct consumer cellular contracts. With over 10.3 million existing Starlink broadband subscribers as a built-in cross-selling base, the orbital giant possesses pricing power that legacy carriers cannot easily counter.

Operationally, T-Mobile is delivering exceptional results that defy its sliding share price. First-quarter 2026 revenue reached $23.1 billion, up 11% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS hitting $2.27 versus consensus estimates of $2.03, a 12% beat. Core service revenue grew 11% to $18.8 billion, while adjusted EBITDA expanded 12%, prompting management to raise full-year guidance. Despite these stellar fundamentals, TMUS stock has declined roughly 25% over the past twelve months, weighed down by US Cellular integration costs and persistent fears around Starlink's competitive trajectory. This disconnect between operational strength and market sentiment creates a compelling asymmetric setup.

Legacy carriers are mounting an aggressive defensive alliance to counter the orbital threat. T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon launched a direct-to-device joint venture to pool spectrum resources and prevent SpaceX from playing carriers against each other. All three majors have collectively rejected MVNO ground-sharing agreements with Starlink, attempting to delay its consumer rollout through infrastructure restrictions. Meanwhile, Rocket Lab's $8 billion acquisition of Iridium signals broader sector consolidation toward vertically integrated space platforms, while SpaceX's executive-level talks with Charter Communications could route Starlink traffic through extensive ground fiber networks.

sum: Investing.com -- Deutsche Telekom shares slid more than 3% on Thursday after the Wall Street Journal reported that the German telecoms giant is pushing to merge with its U.S. subsidiary T-Mobile.

The decline was the sharpest for the stock since late April, when it was reported that the two companies were in discussions about a potential combination. Deutsche Telekom currently holds a majority stake in T-Mobile U.S., which has grown into the group's dominant earnings engine, contributing nearly two-thirds of total revenue.

According to the Journal, Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges is leading the push. To complete a deal, he would need to win over T-Mobile's minority shareholders, who are said to be skeptical of a transaction that would give them exposure to Deutsche Telekom's lower-margin international operations.

He would also need to secure support from the German government, which holds a 28% stake in Deutsche Telekom, before navigating a complex regulatory process that could involve national security reviews in both Germany and the United States, the report said.

Höttges has at times had to balance competing political pressures on both sides of the Atlantic. T-Mobile has cultivated ties with the Trump administration, while decisions made in that context — including the company's withdrawal from diversity, equity and inclusion commitments last year, a move that drew thousands of complaint emails from German shareholders — have created friction at home, the Journal said.
The CEO is expected to retire at the end of 2028 and is said to want the merger completed and a suitable successor in place before he steps down.

sum: Oil rose sharply, and US and European stocks fell after US President Donald Trump said in his first national address since the Iran war began that the US would continue to hit Iran and "finish the job".

Instead of declaring victory or offering clarity on his strategy in the Iran war, the US president promised fresh attacks over the next two to three weeks, reviving fears of rising inflation and slowing economic growth.

Dampened hopes for an end to the war in Iran weighed on stock markets worldwide and gave oil prices a fresh boost early on Thursday. In a rare move, the US benchmark, WTI crude, traded above Brent crude — the global seaborne benchmark and the one most affected by the Iran conflict so far.

“The fact that traders are now prepared to pay a premium for WTI suggests they are becoming worried about the deliverability of seaborne oil — Brent — and scrambling for what they see as a more reliable option, namely WTI,” said Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell.
“This, in turn, suggests traders are starting to position themselves for a conflict that is longer and more drawn out than hoped.”
Nearing 3 p.m. CET, WTI was up 11.5%, at over $111 per barrel, while Brent front-month futures traded at $108.90 per barrel, up more than 7.6%.

In his prime-time speech to Americans, Donald Trump said, “We are going to hit them extremely hard over the next two to three weeks. We’re going to bring them back to the Stone Ages, where they belong.”

items.t: Earnings Preview: What To Expect From T-Mobile's Report
sum: Bellevue, Washington-based T-Mobile US, Inc. (TMUS) provides wireless communications services in the United States and internationally and operates as a subsidiary of Deutsche Telekom AG. The company has a market cap of $231.4 billion and offers voice, messaging, and data services to postpaid, prepaid, wholesale and other services customers.

TMUS is expected to release its Q1 2026 earnings on Tuesday, April 28, after the market closes. Ahead of the event, analysts expect the company's EPS to be $2.27 on a diluted basis, down by 12% from $2.58 in the year-ago quarter. The company has exceeded Wall Street's EPS estimates in each of its last four quarters.

sum: LONDON — European stocks closed mixed on Thursday, as corporate earnings took the spotlight.
While the pan-European Stoxx 600 finished the session just below the flatline, most major bourses ended the day in positive territory.

It was a busy day for earnings in Europe with Deutsche Telekom, Schneider Electric, Allianz, AXA, Munich Re, Engie, Eni, Saint-Gobain, London Stock Exchange Group, Stellantis and Covestro among the firms reporting on Thursday.

German sportswear giant Puma published its full-year earnings for 2025 on Thursday morning, reporting a 13.1% decline in sales that it attributed to its strategy "reset," which was completed last year. The company also pointed to currencies being a headwind. Shares ended the day more than 9% higher.

The firm reported an operating loss of 357.2 million euros ($421.8 million), down from an operating profit of 548.7 million the previous year. The loss was narrower than the 374.3 million euro loss anticipated in an analyst consensus provided by Puma.

Puma said sales declined notably in the second half of the year, while its profit margin fell by 260 basis points to 45%. It proposed canceling dividend payouts for 2025, and said it expected to report an operating loss of between 50 million and 150 million euros this year.

In a Thursday note, analysts at Jefferies said the earnings report showed Puma had made progress "slightly ahead of the journey mapped out in the closing stages of 2025" with "no major surprises from a tough end to 2025."

Want to invest like a Catholic? The Vatican has a new stock index for that.
sum: Looking for divine intervention to boost your stock portfolio? Two new stock indexes from the Vatican may not promise such miracles — but they will help you invest in accordance with Catholic values, Vatican Bank said on Tuesday.

In partnership with Morningstar Indexes, the bank announced indexes for both the European and US markets: the Morningstar IOR US Catholic Principles index and the Morningstar IOR Eurozone Catholic Principles index.

A statement from the bank said the indexes are "built following market best practices and in accordance with Catholic ethical criteria, and are designed to serve as a reference for Catholic investments worldwide."

The bank did not share its criteria for selecting stocks that align with Catholic Social Teaching, but all of the stocks in the indexes are pulled from the Morningstar US Large-Mid Index and the Morningstar Eurozone Large-Mid Index.

When backtested over the last decade, both portfolios, which contain 50 stocks each, have posted impressive gains. The US index has returned 18% per year on average over the last 10 years, while the European index has returned an average of 10.2%.

The largest 10 holdings for the US index include: Meta (5.31%), Amazon (5.22%), Nvidia (5.09%), Tesla (4.84%), Apple (4.62%), JPMorgan (4.27%), Broadcom (4.09%), Visa (3.35%), Micron (3.01%), and Alphabet (2.86%).

Top holdings for the European index include: ASML (6.16%), Deutsche Telekom (5.07%), SAP (3.96%), Banco Santander (3.88%), Hermes (3.82%), Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (3.8%), Prosus (3.76%), Vinci (3.46%), UniCredit (3.45%), and Allianz (3.43%).
